body:
**Stable key:** `MEM-P14`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P13` (#3461)

### Objective

Extend the system beyond caches so bursts, slow consumers, and temporary work cannot escape resource accounting.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements stage P14 of the user-supplied memory-governance report (version 1.0, 2026-09-15). The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No rewrite of business objects into pointer graphs, arbitrary required-message dropping, external database allocator control, or alternate queue topology is included.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R | `Existing request scratch, encoder, compression, database-materialization, and buffer-pool owners` | Concrete paths must be resolved and inventoried in P00. |
| R | `Existing WebSocket sender, fanout, and per-connection queue owners` | Preserve established delivery and replay authority. |
| R | `Existing bounded-channel delivery and drain catalogs` | Register each new queue and its physical owner. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Accounting/` | Workload classes and pool-capacity integration. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Lifetime/` | Per-recipient and shared-operation ownership adapters. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **P14.1** Classify actual large allocations into request scratch, encoding, compression, database materialization, socket send, WebSocket fanout, background build, and recovery. Attach quota, priority, ownership, and measurement at real allocation points, not arbitrary estimates on every Task.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC01`.
- [ ] **P14.2** Account for actual rented bucket capacity and retained pool capacity. Own pools have finite retention and trim policies; third-party retention that cannot be controlled stays observable with explicit headroom. Prevent independent pools from each claiming all spare memory.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC02`.
- [ ] **P14.3** Apply admission before large database result materialization and enforce registered row/string/frame/workspace bounds. Use bounded streaming where the existing protocol permits it while preserving transaction, order, authorization, and cancellation semantics.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC03`.
- [ ] **P14.4** Share only identical qualified immutable WebSocket payloads. Give each recipient a lease and finite queue-count, byte, and deadline bounds. Slow-recipient handling follows the existing delivery classification and must not arbitrarily drop required work.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC04`.
- [ ] **P14.5** Register migration, trimming, transfer completion, and other new queues with the existing bounded-delivery/drain catalog. Include rejected, canceled, replay-pending, detached-producer, and in-flight items in resource ownership.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC05`, `MEM-P14-AC06`.
- [ ] **P14.6** Keep an explicit boundary for CLR, Kestrel, native libraries, kernel buffers, and external processes. Reserve/observe their overhead and reduce controlled work when needed. Do not claim to control PostgreSQL or Redis internal allocators or modify their settings during pressure.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P14-AC08`, `MEM-P14-AC09`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC01** The P00 allocation-family denominator is reconciled after integration. Every in-scope controllable family is connected to admission and ownership; exclusions remain explicit with measurable observation/headroom obligations, not an undefined most-buffers completion claim.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC02** T08 verifies rent, lease return, retention, and trim against independent events. Returned buffers retained by a pool remain charged and sensitive-buffer clearing obeys the original data-class contract.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC03** Database oversize-result and admission-rejection fixtures stop before unbounded materialization. Canonical transaction, sorting, authorization, and result semantics remain unchanged.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC04** T40 verifies one physical payload with multiple recipient leases, independently bounded count and bytes per connection, and the exact existing timeout/backpressure/replay disposition for a slow recipient.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC05** T41 covers queued, in-flight, required, coalescible, and replay-pending work during shutdown. The registered owner proves its terminal disposition before backing is released; queue length zero alone is insufficient.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC06** Canceled or rejected work does not leak payloads or spawn detached uncharged producers. Repeated cancellation and fanout bursts cannot exceed registered queue or workspace hard limits.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC07** With omitted capability settings, eligible pooling/sharing/backing adapters participate automatically; disabling an optimization retains all queue bounds, reservations, and delivery obligations.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC08** External and runtime overhead is labeled observed/estimated rather than exactly controlled. No controller attempts to change external database cache settings or grant itself the host's entire remaining memory.
- [ ] **MEM-P14-AC09** Burst, slow-client, and simultaneous-rebuild tests satisfy the frozen capacity and tail-latency gates with the same delivery/result mix. Faster results caused by dropping additional required messages fail acceptance.

### Required validation scope

Current-stage contract and actual integration tests for the implementation in this issue. Real platform/device evidence is mandatory for every support row this issue claims.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `T01`: Concurrent requests for the final host budget | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P03 | Accepted unique charges plus unconsumed reservations never exceed the configured hard gate; failed requests leave no partial grant. |
| `T08`: Pool rent, return, retention, and trim | Primary implementation owner | Lease return is distinct from retained ownership and OS reclamation; retained capacity stays charged. |
| `T10`: Transport write remains incomplete while the snapshot retires | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | No release before actual consumer completion; eventual release after all remaining holds end. |
| `T11`: Outer wait cancels while underlying work continues | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | Cancellation does not return source, staging, context, or operation reservations before actual completion. |
| `T12`: One singleflight waiter cancels while others remain | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | The shared producer retains resources independently; no unbounded duplicate producers and no corruption of remaining consumers. |
| `T14`: Many publications while an old reader remains active | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | All retained capacity stays charged; new work may be rejected and old data must not be force-freed. |
| `T40`: Large WebSocket fanout with a very slow recipient | Primary implementation owner | One qualified payload may be shared, but per-connection queues and leases obey finite count/byte/deadline and delivery bounds. |
| `T41`: Shutdown with queued, in-flight, and replay-pending payloads | Primary implementation owner | Follow registered drain/delivery classifications; no loss of required work and no early release. |
| `T53`: Continuous pressure events and diagnostics | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P20 | Bound buffers, log volume, and label cardinality and prevent private-data disclosure. |
| `T56`: Repeated build, retirement, compaction, migration, and recovery | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P19 | No unexplained persistent ownership growth; explain retained capacity using actual events. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

Disable only the selected new backing or sharing strategy for future work. Preserve hard admission, finite queues, live leases, and the established transaction and delivery rules.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.
title: [HIGH DIFFICULTY] [MEM-P14] Govern transient buffers, pools, database materialization, and WebSocket fanout
